data.text:
Malawi Airlines pull up your socks. The 2025 report card is out, and your name is missing:

--

Qatar Airways, which in 2025 was named the world’s best airline by air transport rating organization Skytrax, added another award to its shelf by being named the Platinum Winner airline.

Last year the airline delivered 84.42% on-time performance, up from 82.83% in 2024, across 198,303 flights.

Philippine Airlines was No.1 in Asia Pacific, with 83.12% punctuality across 116,268 flights. Cirium notes that this achievement was particularly impressive as the airline’s home base, Manila Ninoy Aquino International, is prone to congestion.

Delta Air Lines took the No. 1 crown in North America, with 80.9% punctuality across more than 1.8 million flights. US airlines this year battled with repeated air traffic control system problems, as well as the 43-day government shutdown, but Cirium declared Delta a model of resiliency in these challenging times.

For the third year in a row, Spain’s Iberia Express was Europe’s No. 1 airline. It achieved 88.94% punctuality across 37,119 flights, despite facing obstacles such as a major power outage affecting air travel across the Iberian Peninsula and a global software issue impacting its fleet of Airbus A320s.

Panamanian flag carrier Copa Airlines was No. 1 in Latin America, delivering 90.75% punctuality across 133,748 flights. Cirium says the region is emerging as one of the “most dynamic” in global aviation, expected to account for 8.5% of global passenger traffic in 2025, according to projections by Airports Council International (ACI).

South Africa’s FlySafair was the leading airline in the Middle East and Africa, achieving 91.06% punctuality across 62,805 flights.

--

Source: CNN

data.text:
Handa ang Metropolitan Manila Development Authority (MMDA) katuwang ang iba’t ibang ahensiya para sa Traslacion 2026 ngayong Enero 9, kung saan inaasahang dadalo ang milyon-milyong deboto.

Ipinahayag ni General Manager Nicolas Torre ang buong suporta ng ahensiya sa Pista ng Hesus Nazareno, kabilang ang paglalagay ng mga kinakailangang barrier at portable toilets, pati na ang pagsasagawa ng cleanup operations matapos ang prusisyon upang mapanatili ang kaayusan at kalinisan sa dadaanan ng Traslacion.

Pinasalamatan naman ni Manila Mayor Isko Moreno ang lahat ng katuwang na ahensiya na sa pagpapatupad ng mga kinakailangang hakbang para sa seguridad at kaayusan ng pagdiriwang. Pinaalala niya rin sa publiko na mahigpit na ipinagbabawal ang paggamit ng paputok sa lungsod habang Traslacion.

Nanawagan naman si Department of Health (DOH) Asec. Gloria Balboa sa publiko na isaalang-alang ang kalusugan at kaligtasan, at kung maaari ay huwag nang dumalo ang mga bata, buntis, senior citizens, immuno-compromised, at may karamdaman sa Traslacion. Hinimok din niya ang mga deboto na magdala ng pagkain, tubig, at kanilang gamot kinakailangang gamoy upang maiwasan ang anumang suliraning pangkalusugan.

Nakahanda ang hanay ng Saint John the Baptist Church at mga katuwang na ahensya upang masiguro ang maayos at ligtas na pagdalo ng mga deboto.

Ipinaalala naman nina Reverend Father Ramon  Licuanan at Robert Arellano, LRMS na ang tunay na diwa ng Traslacion ay nakaugnay sa debosyon at pagsisimba sa Poong Nazareno, at hindi lamang sa pakikibahagi sa prusisyon. Hinikayat niya ang lahat ng deboto na makiisa nang may disiplina, pananagutan, at paggalang sa kapwa, sa patuloy na pagdiriwang ng isang tradisyong malalim na nakaugat sa kulturang Pilipino at pananampalataya.

Dumalo rin sa pulong sina MMDA Traffic Discipline Office Director for Enforcement Atty. Victor Nuñez, Quiapo Church Adviser Alex Irasga, Manila Vice Mayor Angela Atienza, MPD DDD PCOL Emil Tumibay, at OCD-NCR Regional Director George Keyser.
